Findings-triage round (#4949 discipline): **promoted** — `finding` → `pm:queue`, `domain:metadata` kept.

- **Stale-premise check (`origin/main` @ `3172831`)**: premise holds — `classifyIndexFailure` at `packages/metadata-protocol/src/migrations/view-definition-active-index.ts:278` still takes `message: string` only and still answers the unique-violation question with its own private regex at `:279`. The shared predicate (`packages/types/src/unique-violation.ts`) exists and is unconsumed here.
- **Why promote rather than hold**: this is a member of the active #6250 convergence program, not a standalone observation — sibling #6543 (`driver-sql`'s copy) sits queued in `domain:drivers`, and #6544 (`import-runner`'s copy) already landed. The fix shape is bounded and stated in the body (pass the caught error down, `isUniqueViolationError(error)` for the first arm only, ordering preserved), one consumer per PR per the family's lane discipline. Leaving the fifth vocabulary out of the program it was inventoried against is drift, not thrift.
- **Two load-bearing constraints for the dispatch prompt**: arm ordering stays (duplicate wording before dialect wording), and the real work is threading the error object from the caller (`:369`) — a string-only swap discards the `code`/`errno`/`cause` channels that justify the migration.
- **Dedup**: #6250 / #6543 / #6544 are the family, each a distinct consumer; no in-flight PR touches `view-definition-active-index.ts` (checked open PRs). No serial constraint.
- **Release board**: no `target:*` — the message superset covers all three shipped dialects today; the hole needs a code/errno-only driver report to land.

本评论来自分诊座位 Routine（#5474 试点），不构成认领。

**os-dev report — #6699** · status `done` · PR #6845 (draft) · branch `claude/issue-6699-classify-index-failure-error-channel`

## Premise: valid, but the card's file anchor had expired

The issue body and the 14:29Z triage comment both place `classifyIndexFailure` at `view-definition-active-index.ts:279`. On `origin/main` @ `220536377` it is **not there** — #6418 moved it to `migrations/partial-index-probe.ts:102` when `ensureOverlayIndex` adopted the probe-first order; `view-definition-active-index.ts:196` only re-exports it now. This is a bigger drift than the claim comment anticipated (it warned about line anchors moving under PR #6817, not about the function having changed file).

Everything the finding asserts holds at the new address: still `classifyIndexFailure(message: string)`, still its own private regex, and `isUniqueViolationError` still had zero consumers in this package. So `premise_still_valid: true` — the fix simply landed one file over.

Two consequences of the move, both recorded in the PR:

- **The vocabulary is shared by BOTH migrations.** `view-definition-active-index.ts` and `overlay-index.ts` classify through the one `probeThenReplaceIndex` call site, so there is exactly one threading point and both migrations are fixed by it. Still one consumer in the #6250 family sense — one vocabulary, one PR.
- **`overlay-index.ts` ACTS on the verdict**, it does not only report it: its `unsupported` branch builds a composite fallback lookup index. A conflict misclassified as `unsupported` therefore also built an index nobody asked for.

## PM mechanism assumptions — measured

| assumption | result |
|:---|:---|
| base ≥ `50a8d115a` | confirmed, branched from `220536377` |
| `classifyIndexFailure` string-only, predicate unconsumed here | confirmed (at the new path) |
| callers = one in-file site (~`:369`) + tests | **falsified** — the only call site is `probeThenReplaceIndex`'s `catch` in `partial-index-probe.ts`, reached by both migrations; plus the `index.ts` public re-export and two test files. Full-repo grep in the PR. |
| `isUniqueViolationError` takes string or object, reads `code`/`errno`/`cause`/`message` | confirmed by reading `packages/types/src/unique-violation.ts`. Named export, `(error: unknown) =. boolean`, cause walk bounded at depth 4. Contract sufficient — no `packages/types` edit, no STOP needed. |

## What changed

First arm delegates to `isUniqueViolationError`; `probeThenReplaceIndex` passes the **caught error object** rather than `err.message`. `detail` is untouched — still the driver's prose, for the operator. Signature widens `string` to `unknown`, so every existing string call compiles and is judged identically.

**Both load-bearing constraints preserved.** Arm order unchanged (duplicate/unique before dialect, with the doc comment's rationale kept and extended). Dialect arm untouched and still this module's own message-based vocabulary, reading via a new private `indexFailureText` that prefers `message` and falls back to `String()` — a bare string resolves to itself.

Measured old-versus-new: all 6 message-channel verdicts unchanged; 6 object-channel cases move from `failed`/`unsupported` to `conflict` (SQLite `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE`, MySQL `ER_DUP_ENTRY`/errno 1062, bare errno, Postgres `23505`, a `cause`-wrapped `23505`, and code-plus-dialect-wording). Full table in the PR.

## Reverse verification — direction predicted first, split in two

**Stage A**, revert only the call-site threading: predicted exactly one red — the threading pin — because no classifier-level assertion can see how the caller calls it. Result: `1 failed | 754 passed`, `the probe hands the ERROR to the classifier` → `expected 'failed' to be 'conflict'`.

**Stage B**, revert the whole source file to `origin/main`: predicted all object-channel pins red, all prose pins green. Result: `8 failed | 747 passed`, all 8 object-channel, every prose pin green.

One prediction reported honestly rather than dressed up: `a dialect refusal carrying its own code is still 'unsupported'` is green in **both** directions by design — it pins that widening the input did not blind the second arm, so it can never be evidence the fix works.

## Tests and gates

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/metadata-protocol test` → **63 files, 755 tests, all pass**. `tsc --noEmit` → 0 errors in the changed files; package total 63, exactly its DEBT ledger entry, so the ratchet does not move. `eslint` clean. `check:nul-bytes`, `check:durability-log-level`, `check:adr-anchors`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:empty-changeset`, `check:startup-registry-verdict`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:type-check-coverage` all pass. `check:type-check-debt` refuses to run locally without a full build closure (its own #6376 guard) and was left to CI.

**CI converged, 24 check runs, 22 success + 2 skipped, 0 failures.** Per-job conclusions read individually: `ESLint` success, `TypeScript Type Check` success (this is where the debt ratchet ran with the closure built), `Check Changeset` success, `Test Core` and all three shards success.

Changeset: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` patch. `skip-changeset` not applicable — a changeset is present.

## Out of scope

Filed **#6848** (`finding`, unassigned, no `pm:queue`): the two arms now read different depths — `isUniqueViolationError` walks `cause`, the dialect arm reads the outer message only. Dormant (no shipped driver wraps DDL errors that way) and not a regression from this PR, but if a wrapping driver ever lands, `overlay-index.ts` silently skips its fallback lookup index rather than merely wording the report differently.
